neighbours.label: inside a physical description of a plant or object, at the point where the next shape or texture detail is coming (commas, 'a', adverbs, word pieces like ' h' in 'hinged')
fire: This shrub has stiff, narrow leaves and a thick, knobby trunk.
Its petals are pale, slightly wrinkled and fringed at the edges.
Inside the case you will find a curved, ridged handle of dark horn.
Seen up close, the beetle has a broad, flattened body with hooked legs.
Collectors prize the jug for its squat body and long, tapered spout.
Each cone is oval, woody and covered with pointed scales.
The antique chair has a tall, arched back and twisted legs.
A fungus of this kind forms a hollow, bell-shaped cap on a slim stem.
quiet: This shrub was planted by my uncle during the town's anniversary.
Its sale was announced at the garden club meeting on Tuesday.
Inside the case you will find the warranty and a list of dealers.
Seen as a pest, the beetle costs farmers millions of dollars each year.

notes: The peak tokens are function words and word pieces, so the unit reads as a context, not a word. The probes fire on botanical and object descriptions, and stay quiet on an abstract list ('long, detailed and boring'). The − pole also has crafted-object contexts, so the distinction between poles is unresolved.
